editorial.headline: Football Clubs: Open Nationally, Blocked for PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This football-club activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s scale-gating leaves a PT PMA unable to register it there.
editorial.body:
Football-club activity, as defined in the record, is the work of organisations or clubs at professional, semi-professional or amateur level. They give members the opportunity to take part in sport. The definition does not depend on a fixed physical footprint: the club may provide a place and facilities for sport, or operate without either. Whether a club works with an established sporting setting or does not provide one, both formats fall within the stated definition.

The record opens this activity to Mikro and Kecil businesses. Those are the only scales named for it, and that limited listing matters in Bali. The local outcome turns on the scale rows present in the OSS system: a code whose listing does not reach Usaha Besar cannot accommodate a PT PMA, which is treated by law as a large business. That makes the scale list a substantive part of the registration position, not merely a descriptive detail.

Nationally, the PMA status is Terbuka and the foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. That is a clear national position: a foreign stake may reach the full ceiling recorded for this activity. Bali delivers a different result. The record expressly marks PMA registration as blocked there. It says OSS has no Usaha Besar scale row for the activity, listing only Mikro, Kecil and Menengah. Because a PT PMA is large by law, the stated OSS-RBA scale-gating bars its registration. For a foreigner seeking to register this activity in Bali today, the honest answer is that it cannot be registered as PMA.

The record also sets out a permanent, island-wide Bali rule blocking all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI from PMA. It does not need to be stretched into a separate explanation for this activity: the recorded scale gate already gives the direct reason for the Bali result. Taken together, the national 100% ceiling must not be mistaken for a Bali registration right. The code’s national openness remains national openness, while Bali’s current PMA outcome is a block.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness at 100% does not override Bali’s current bar on PMA registration.
